notes: The italic and between בְּתוֹךְ אֶפְרַיִם and בְּתוֹךְ מְנַשֶּׁה answers to no conjunction morpheme and is added under rule 14's closing sentences; the italic corroborates without deciding (rule 7).
בְּתוֹךְ is split rather than fused, because the ASV writes in for the preposition and the midst for the construct noun, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet (rule 2).
אֶת before אֶפְרָיִם in וַיִּלָּחֶם אֶת־אֶפְרָיִם is the homograph preposition with (H854) and aligns ordinarily, while the two object markers are unrepresented (rule 16).
The copula are joins the nominal predicate פְּלִיטֵי and the explicit אַתֶּם keeps only Ye (rule 20); the vocative גִּלְעָד takes the supplied ye into its own unit (rule 36).
